subject: chemistry
title: Oxidation and reduction (oxygen)
key_idea: Metals react with oxygen to form metal oxides. This is oxidation, because the metal gains oxygen. Reduction is the opposite: loss of oxygen. The two always happen together in a redox reaction.

blocks.text: This section covers what happens when a metal is heated in air or oxygen.

items: Metals react with oxygen to produce **metal oxides**.
The metal gains oxygen, so the reaction is an **oxidation** reaction.
The metal oxide is a compound of the metal and oxygen only.
Magnesium burns with a bright white flame and leaves white magnesium oxide.

blocks.label: Symbol equations for metals and oxygen
where: Mg, Na, Fe: magnesium, sodium, iron
MgO, Na₂O, Fe₂O₃: the metal oxides

items: The metal is oxidised because it gains oxygen.

blocks.text: This section covers the two definitions in terms of oxygen and how to use them on an equation.

items.meaning: A reaction in which oxidation and reduction happen at the same time.

items.lead: Find the substance that gains oxygen.
Find the substance that loses oxygen.

items.text: In a metal oxide, say the oxide (for example iron oxide) is reduced, not just the metal.

blocks.text: In 2CuO + C → 2Cu + CO₂, copper oxide loses oxygen and carbon gains it.

items: Copper oxide (CuO) is **reduced**, because it loses oxygen.
Carbon (C) is **oxidised**, because it gains oxygen to form carbon dioxide.
Oxygen is transferred from one substance to the other, so the reaction is a redox reaction.

diagram.alt: Sort each change into oxidation or reduction.
diagram.prompt: Is the substance oxidised or reduced?

items.text: Tin oxide in SnO₂ + C → Sn + CO₂

items: Oxidation is gain of oxygen. Reduction is loss of oxygen.
Oxidation and reduction happen together in a redox reaction.
Say which substance gains or loses oxygen, and name the whole substance.

blocks.text: A metal heated in a crucible gains mass as it gains oxygen.

items.text: Find the mass of the empty crucible and lid, then add the metal and weigh again.
Heat strongly. Lift the lid from time to time to let air in.
Heat to constant mass, then weigh the crucible, lid and product.
Final mass of oxide minus start mass of metal is the mass of oxygen that combined.

items: The oxide is heavier than the metal, because oxygen has been added.
Without a lid, some of the metal oxide escapes as smoke, so the mass of oxide collected is less.
Mass of oxide is greater than the mass of metal, because oxygen has been gained.
Keep a lid on the crucible so no product escapes.

checks.q: Magnesium burns in oxygen to form magnesium oxide. Is the magnesium oxidised or reduced? Give a reason.
Lead oxide is heated with carbon: 2PbO + C → 2Pb + CO₂. Which substance is reduced?
checks.a: Lead oxide (PbO), because it loses oxygen.

checks.q: Why is the mass of a metal greater after it has been heated in air?
checks.a: The metal has gained oxygen to form the metal oxide.

mistakes.wrong: Iron oxide is reduced because it gains electrons.
mistakes.right: When the question says answer in terms of oxygen, references to gain of electrons are ignored. Say iron oxide loses oxygen.

mistakes.wrong: Carbon is reduced because it takes oxygen from the oxide.
mistakes.right: The reason mark depends on naming the right substance. Carbon gains oxygen, so it is oxidised. The oxide that loses oxygen is reduced.

mistakes.wrong: Without a lid the mass of magnesium oxide would be greater, because more air gets in.
mistakes.right: Without a lid the mass of magnesium oxide is less, because some of the product escaped.

worked_example.question:
Tin (Sn) is extracted from tin oxide using carbon. The equation for the reaction is:

SnO₂ + C → Sn + CO₂

Which substance is reduced in this reaction?

Give one reason for your answer.

Answer in terms of oxygen.
worked_example.tip: The reason mark is only given if you named the right substance first.

exam_phrases: carbon gained oxygen (to form carbon dioxide)
reject other elements (for the substance oxidised)

mistakes.wrong: Oxidation is when oxygen reacts with a metal.
mistakes.right: Oxygen reacts with metal is ignored. Say oxidation is the gain of oxygen.

mistakes.wrong: In 2PbO + C → 2Pb + CO₂, lead is oxidised.
mistakes.right: Other elements are rejected. Carbon is oxidised because it gains oxygen to form carbon dioxide.

mistakes.wrong: Iron is reduced when it reacts with oxygen to form iron oxide.
mistakes.right: Iron gains oxygen, so it is oxidised. Reduction is loss of oxygen.

worked_example.question:
In one stage of the extraction of lead from its ore, lead oxide is heated strongly with carbon.

The equation for the reaction is

2PbO + C → 2Pb + CO₂

Explain, using this equation, which substance has been oxidised in this reaction.
answer_points: It gained oxygen (to form carbon dioxide).
worked_example.tip: Other elements are rejected for the first mark. Oxidation as loss of electrons is also allowed.

exam_phrases: copper oxide / CuO loses oxygen or is reduced
carbon / C gains oxygen or is oxidised
the oxidising agent is oxygen and the reducing agent is magnesium

mistakes.right: Do not allow this. Copper oxide loses oxygen, and copper is what is left.

mistakes.wrong: Iron oxide is reduced because iron is formed.
mistakes.right: The mark is for the process, not the products. Say oxygen is removed from iron oxide. Saying iron is formed is ignored.

mistakes.wrong: Hydrogen is oxidised because water is formed.
mistakes.right: Water is formed is ignored. Say hydrogen gains oxygen.

worked_example.question:
Copper is extracted by heating copper oxide with carbon.

2CuO + C → 2Cu + CO₂

Explain why this is an example of a redox reaction.
answer_points: Copper oxide (CuO) loses oxygen, so it is reduced.
Carbon (C) gains oxygen, so it is oxidised.
worked_example.tip: A redox reaction needs both. Do not say that copper loses oxygen.

blocks.text: OCR also asks which substance is the oxidising agent and which is the reducing agent.

items.meaning: The substance that oxidises another substance. It is itself reduced.
The substance that reduces another substance. It is itself oxidised.

items: In 2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO the oxidising agent is oxygen and the reducing agent is magnesium.
In Mg + CuO → MgO + Cu the reducing agent is magnesium, because it takes oxygen from copper oxide.
